title: Leveraging existing sparse point annotations for benthic imagery dense segmentation
abstract: arXiv:2608.17561v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: The health of marine ecosystems is a critical indicator of global environmental change, yet the physical constraints of underwater observation and the intrinsic challenges of processing marine imagery severely limit the scalability of systematic monitoring. While recent visual foundation models such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM) series show great promise, they still struggle with the fine-grained recognition required in these complex scenarios and still require expert supervision. Our work addresses this gap by bridging state-of-the-art foundation models with existing sparse supervision. Because historical benthic surveys are typically annotated with only a few sparse expert points per image, we utilize these legacy point-labels as visual prompts for SAM2. Our primary contribution is a novel mechanism to automatically identify which of these points are suitable, and which are actively harmful, when used for propagation. By filter

translated_title: 利用现有稀疏点标注实现海底影像密集分割
translated_abstract: 摘要：海洋生态系统的健康是全球环境变化的关键指标，然而水下观测的物理限制以及海洋影像处理的固有挑战严重制约了系统化监测的可扩展性。尽管近期诸如Segment Anything Model（SAM）系列等视觉基础模型展现出巨大潜力，但它们在这些复杂场景中所需的细粒度识别方面仍显不足，且仍需专家监督。我们的工作通过将最先进的基础模型与现有稀疏监督相结合，填补了这一空白。由于历史海底调查通常每张图像仅标注少量稀疏专家点，我们利用这些遗留的点标签作为SAM2的视觉提示。我们的主要贡献是一种新颖机制，用于自动识别这些点在用于传播时哪些是合适的，哪些是有害的，并通过过滤来优化使用。
tldr: 本文提出一种自动过滤机制，利用历史海底调查中的稀疏专家点标签作为SAM2的视觉提示，实现无需额外专家监督的密集分割，并识别有害点以提升性能。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes an automatic filtering mechanism that uses sparse expert point labels from historical benthic surveys as visual prompts for SAM2, enabling dense segmentation without additional expert supervision while identifying harmful points to improve performance.
